title: Peter Todd Hash Collision Bounties

prize.note: combined across 4 live P2SH scripts (SHA-256, RIPEMD-160, HASH160, HASH256); a 5th sibling (SHA-1) was claimed in 2023 and is not part of this total

addresses.label: SHA-1 (reference sibling, claimed 2023-02-22, not part of the live prize)

target_format: two distinct byte strings, each under 521 bytes, with equal digest under the named hash function; submitted directly in a scriptSig, no key derivation involved

derivation.summary: supply 2 distinct pushes a, b in a single scriptSig such that HASH(a) == HASH(b); this is the generic collision-finding problem for the named hash, with no shortcut in the script itself
derivation.certified_against: the real 2023-02-22 SHA-1 claim (txid 9ec2a0db0c4c3423a6b2c3cb2a26fc626b037121b4b5f3f57b08916196ff14e0, block 777856), decoded directly from its scriptSig: the SHAttered PDF-prefix pair; and the same-day 2013-09-13 OP_ABS demo claim, a non-hash sibling script proving the same payout template works

difficulty_note: no known shortcut over the generic collision bound for any of the 4 live hash functions (2^128 for SHA-256 and HASH256, 2^80 for RIPEMD-160 and HASH160); what would close this is a published practical collision on one of them, the way SHAttered did for SHA-1 in 2017

leads.title: a published practical or academic full collision on SHA-256, RIPEMD-160, HASH160 or HASH256
RIPEMD-160 and HASH160 as the most-watched sub-targets (smallest generic bound, more active reduced-round literature)
passive monitoring of the spent flag on the 4 live addresses and of collision announcements

third_party_material: the redeem-script table and the quoted lines are Peter Todd's own puzzle material, quoted briefly with source and date; the SHAttered SHA-1 collision pair is a public academic research artifact (Stevens et al., 2017), read directly from the public blockchain rather than reproduced from the paper; no other third-party material is included
